acceptance_criteria.requirement: Mount the spec-defined Dev Command Center reliability view through the existing KernelDcc pane and native app/pane-registry owner. DCC owns control/projection and work/session binding; Operator Consoles retain Problems, Jobs, Timeline and Evidence drilldown. Consume published typed contracts from MT-204 through MT-208. No competing execution state, direct tool launch, new scheduler, supervisor daemon or replacement workflow family.

Show stable job/workflow/node/attempt/owner/session and correlation IDs with backend revision/freshness, original context and governed allowed-action IDs. Distinguish queued, running, cancel requested, cleanup pending, unknown and settled outcomes using backend vocabulary. Liveness, readiness and meaningful progress are separate values with explicit wait reason; local timers, badge color, window presence or empty filters cannot establish job state.

Project MT-204 MCP admission/deadline/reconnect state, MT-205 process ownership/cancellation settlement, MT-206 resource policy and remaining admission/retry budget, MT-207 transition/fence outcomes and MT-208 legacy replay reconciliation. Show health failure, contract mismatch, capability denial and transport loss distinctly. Missing or unpublished contracts produce truthful unavailable/blocked UI only, never invented healthy data.

Cancel, reconcile, retry and recovery controls route through the existing governed backend action contract with original account/Principal/AccessSpace/job/attempt/fence context. Show accepted request separately from confirmed cleanup/settlement. Repeated clicks, delayed acknowledgements and stale rows cannot duplicate mutation. A context switch, logout or revocation invalidates stale actions before dispatch and protected result publication; immutable running context is never silently retargeted.

Closing or crashing an owned GUI window does not imply job death or cancel backend work. Reopen reconstructs the view from authoritative backend records and preserves attempt lineage. Backend outage leaves the native UI responsive with unknown/unavailable state and evidence links; reconnect rereads backend truth before enabling actions. Demonstrate GUI and runtime failure boundaries using the existing separate processes, without a daemon rewrite.

The genuine native GUI consumes the exact published KUMIHIMO-ASSET-001 public contract and actual Vulkan path under MT-199, with central GPU ownership/lifecycle from MT-203. Use small focused GUI modules and typed clients. One GUI writer owns shared app.rs/lib.rs/pane_registry.rs changes. Missing reusable toolkit logic belongs in separate canonical source work before pinned host adoption, never copied into this module.

Preserve all original editor, CKC/PoseKit, orchestration and other affected workflows. Prove keyboard/focus/accessibility, stable model author_id routing, simultaneous Operator/two-agent clients, responsive normal/constrained/DPI layouts, readable state and nonoverlapping controls. Inspect empty/loading/error/denied/unknown/recovery views with Argus or native AccessKit/headless routes and renderer/runtime error scans; zero focus theft.

UserManual and three diagnostic tiers ship with the affected GUI change. Flight Recorder projects governed business actions and evidence; internal_diagnostics records actual GUI/transport/frame failures; standalone Palmistry records genuine owned-process failure evidence and never becomes a controller/recovery executor. Enforce private-resource and metadata isolation in feed filters, counts, tool details, screenshots and evidence links. Independent real GUI/backend acceptance is required; a prototype or mock projection cannot prove integration.

risks: A local badge, hidden row or stale response can misrepresent backend state.
Cancel acknowledgement can be mistaken for physical cleanup or free budget.
View/context switching can apply an old action to a new account or attempt.
GUI loss can accidentally terminate work or encourage a new duplicate run.
Parallel GUI authors can conflict in shared mount files.
Prototype or fallback rendering can be misreported as genuine Vulkan and backend proof.
